prediction: In addition to v1 behavior, when remainder_words==1 the new descriptor store aliases old_header[1] before the copy branch reads that address. Therefore both arg4 modes write the just-stored descriptor value into new_header[1], while the separately saved owner_slot still receives the new payload pointer. V2 changes only the owner-only RHS to read old_header[1] after the descriptor store.
falsifier: Falsify if a fresh target-derived fixture using remainder_words==1 and both arg4 modes disagrees with the post-store alias result, or if any previously covered sizing/header/payload/owner update/helper ordering changes. Only the owner-only RHS is changed in source; no arithmetic or codegen variants.

new_evidence: work/host_pool_shrink/shape_evidence_v1.json records the slot0x28 callback cell, two direct caller stack sequences and owner/header transitions; cross-checked with evidence/host_pool_layout.json and evidence/crt_copy.json.
new_discriminator: At 0x46d0 target sets EDX=ESI-4, the old owner-word address. At 0x46e6 EDI=ESI+remainder*4-8 (new header); at 0x46f6 it stores the new descriptor to [EDI]. For remainder_words==1, EDI==ESI-4, so this overwrites the source word. Only afterward does target branch at0x46fb/0x46fd; arg4==0 passes EDX to memmove at0x4709, while arg4!=0 loads [EDX] at0x4713 and copies that value to [EDI+4] at0x4715. Thus the one-word remainder leaves the new owner-header word equal to the new descriptor, even though EBP captured the real owner_slot earlier and target updates *EBP at0x471a.

metrics.capability: One target-ordering correction to the owner-only store, freshly measured once with pinned VC5 and tested against the new one-word alias fixture plus the prior edge cases.
